subject: Re: Kickoff: MMMT-IF — baseline results + a gating trade-off
body:
Hi both,

Baseline sweep is done. Headline: all three candidate checkpoints degrade sharply with instruction count. With 1–2 active instructions, verifier pass rates sit at 88–91%. By turn 15, with 6+ instructions accumulated in history, the best checkpoint passes 54% and the worst 41%. The failure is retrieval, not reasoning — when we re-inject all active instructions into the final prompt as an oracle, pass rates recover to 85%+. That matches what the paper found; the instructions spread through history are what kills them.

The trade-off for the gate: if we set the threshold at 80% pass over full 20-turn sessions, nothing ships this quarter. My proposal is a two-tier gate — 85% at up-to-4 instructions (hard block) and a published-but-non-blocking score on the full benchmark, tightening each quarter.

tbh the honest read is the models need an instruction-tracking scratchpad, but that's a model-team roadmap item, not an eval item.

Yusuf
